decisions.question: Classify September customer deposits.

decisions.question: Classify New bank borrowing.
decisions.answer: Recognise the €50,000 bank advance as cash and a bank loan.

decisions.aiProposal: Recognise the €50,000 bank advance as cash and a bank loan.
decisions.independentChallenge: The bank receipt cannot be treated as income because it creates a repayment obligation.
decisions.studentReasoning: Confirmed yes by the student: The bank record supports both the cash receipt and the loan balance. Recording only cash would overstate equity.

decisions.question: Classify Packaging machine.
decisions.answer: Capitalise the €60,000 packaging machine as PPE.
evidence: Bank statements, invoices and accounting schedules
decisions.aiProposal: Capitalise the €60,000 packaging machine as PPE.
decisions.independentChallenge: The machine gives a benefit over more than one accounting period, so immediate expensing would understate assets.
decisions.studentReasoning: Confirmed yes by the student: It is a long-life production asset. I capitalised the purchase and charge depreciation over its useful life.

decisions.question: Classify Photo booth.
decisions.answer: Capitalise the €20,000 booth as PPE.

decisions.aiProposal: Capitalise the €20,000 booth as PPE.
decisions.independentChallenge: The booth is reusable equipment, not a one-off event expense.
decisions.studentReasoning: Confirmed yes by the student: It will be used across future events, so I treated it as PPE and included it in the depreciation schedule.

decisions.independentChallenge: The work restores the existing asset rather than creating a new asset or increasing its capacity.
decisions.studentReasoning: Confirmed yes by the student: The description says repair. I expensed it now because the benefit is maintenance of the existing asset.
